bugs.summary: _R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_ assumes that .Library doesn't contain third-party packages
bugs.creator: ikrylov

comments.creator: ikrylov
comments.text:
When checking whether a package works without its `Suggests` available, `R CMD check` prepares a temporary library containing only the stated hard dependencies. It has to keep `.Library` available, which is where the base packages live, and includes this comment (`src/library/tools/R/check.R`, function `setRlibs`):

```
## We need to make some assumptions about layout: this version
## assumes .Library contains standard and recommended packages
## and nothing else.
```

Unfortunately, `.Library` can end up being writeable and therefore collect third-party packages: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2023-July/082740.html

I don't know whether it's been fixed on macOS, but keeping a build of R-devel in a home directory is something that many R package developers do. Having CRAN packages installed under `.Library` makes it impossible to check packages with `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_=TRUE`.

`setRlibs` contains additional logic to test whether a package works without Recommended packages. Since those do live in `.Library`, `setRlibs` sets up empty shells of them in the temporary library that take precedence over `.Library` but fail to load. Can this logic be reused for the regular dependencies under `Suggests:` too? I have duplicated the logic in a very crude manner, and it seems to work, but more testing and better integration with `setRlibs` is needed:

```
if (!suggests) for(pkg in names(pi$Suggests) %w/o% deps) {
    dir.create(pd <- file.path(tmplib, pkg))
    f <- system.file('DESCRIPTION', package = pkg)
    if(file.exists(f)) file.copy(f, pd)
    close(file(file.path(pd, "dummy_for_check"), "w"))
}
```

The fact that this works probably relies on an implementation detail of the package loader. A different solution would be to set up a private, non-API environment variable for the duration of the check `_R_PACKAGE_PROHIBIT_LOADING_=dep1,dep2,...` and consult it when loading packages.

Or is it better to always set up a separate library, even for R-devel?
